title: Plurimath conformance rejection group
description: Inputs the oracle gem REFUSES, so an implementation can be checked on what it must not accept. A positive corpus records only successes, which means a port returning something plausible wherever the gem raises passes every case in `cases/1` and is still wrong. This is a separate payload kind rather than a variant of a case: `expected`, `parse_tree` and `model` are all required there and none of them exists for an input that never parsed, and a rejection group has no `targets` because nothing is rendered.

schema.description: Schema this payload follows. A kind, like `provenance`, not an input format: the format is carried per payload in `input_format`.

group.description: Equals the file's stem; scripts/validate.rb enforces the agreement.

error_category.description: What the gem raised. Only `parse_error` today, and deliberately so: this corpus records bad *inputs*, and every bad input reaches the same public boundary. `Plurimath::Math.parse` rescues everything and re-raises `Math::ParseError` with `cause: nil`, so a grammar failure cannot be told apart from any other parse-time failure from outside. The gem's other errors were probed and come from bad *arguments* rather than bad input (`Math::InvalidTypeError` for an unknown format, `Math::ParseOptionError` for a bad `formatter:`, `Errors::UnsupportedLocale` for a bad `locale:`), which is a different axis this corpus does not cover. Naming them here would put values in a shared contract that nothing produces; a later kind of case gets a schema version instead.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the group; scripts/validate.rb enforces the uniqueness, which one schema item cannot see of its siblings.

input.description: The input as written. Never empty: an implementation has to be given something to refuse.

input_format.description: Equals the group's `input_format`; scripts/validate.rb enforces the agreement.

preprocessed.description: The input after the format's preprocessing pass. Recorded because `index` is an offset into THIS text, not into `input`: AsciiMath's parser rewrites `{:` and friends to single characters before parsing, which shifts every later offset. Each implementation maps back through its own offset map.

index.description: Character offset into `preprocessed` where the parse failed, when the gem exposed one. The public `Math::ParseError` carries no position, so this comes from the `Parslet::ParseFailed` underneath it — but NOT from `parse_failure_cause.pos` directly, which is 0 for every rejection recorded here because the root cause is the whole-input rule. The generator walks that cause tree and takes the furthest position any branch reached, which is the offset a reader means by "where it failed". Absent whenever the failure did not come from the grammar at all.

error.description: What the gem did, at the coarseness its public boundary exposes. The gem's message is deliberately NOT recorded: it is a multi-line banner carrying an issue-tracker URL, no consumer may assert on it, and embedding it would make an upstream wording change rewrite every payload's bytes and every provenance digest without a single conformance change.
